referents.why: 'my feet' is the psalm's own voice, which a first person in a psalm names, but no voice candidate is offered; the only person candidate is the LORD, which does not fit a first person speaker.
second person masculine singular; the psalm is addressed to God throughout, and the LORD (masculine singular) is the addressee the candidates offer.
referents.category: second person addressee of the psalm

referents.why: 'my path' is the psalm's own voice, as w3; no voice candidate is offered.

links.why: plain waw (וְ) joining two parallel lines; the sense is neither cause, result nor purpose, so it stays a plain 'and'.

groups.why: cl1 'a light to my path' restates the roles of cl0 'a lamp to my feet' with no subject of its own; the subject, 'your word' (w4), is the same in both.

none_fit.where: slots w3 and w10 (my feet, my path)
none_fit.what: the rules name the psalm's own voice (a voice candidate) for a first person in a psalm, but this verse offers no voice candidate; recorded as none rather than forced onto the LORD.
